title: Thread ledger: checkpoints and entries bound to a story

story.as_a: orchestrator or runner session working a delivery story
story.i_want_to: record each checkpoint and each reasoning, finding, fix and verdict entry against the story's thread
story.so_that: a reviewer and Mark read a change's reasoning next to its diff, in one place, without a pull request

rationale: loopctl holds everything around a change except the change; PRD §3.

acceptance_criteria.description: A thread_checkpoints table (tenant_id, story_id, seq, commit_sha, tree_sha, parent_checkpoint_id, kind checkpoint|base_update, claim_epoch, dispatch_id, merge_commit_sha, gate_evidence map, inserted_at) exists with RLS enabled, unique (story_id, seq) and unique (story_id, commit_sha, claim_epoch).

A thread_entries table (tenant_id, story_id, seq, kind, author_principal, dispatch_id, idempotency_key NOT NULL, body, checkpoint_id, inserted_at) exists with RLS enabled, unique (story_id, seq) and unique (story_id, author_principal, idempotency_key); the kind column admits message, checkpoint, review_requested, finding, fix, verdict, escalation and merge.

Recording a checkpoint is refused with 409 not_claimant, stale_claim_epoch or claim_not_live unless the caller is the story's current claimant (Delivery.Claimant) under the current claim_epoch while the claim is live: a claimed status, a lease not passed, and no review requested (Progress.live_claim? plus the review marker). The recorder's resend of the same (commit_sha, claim_epoch) with the same tree and note returns the recorded checkpoint with 200 even after the claim ends; another tree or note is 409 checkpoint_conflict; the same commit under a new claim is recorded again, with no parent from the ended claim; commit and tree must share one object format. Each checkpoint's audit-chain event records its commit_sha, tree_sha and claim_epoch.

Re-sending an entry with the same idempotency_key and the same kind, body and checkpoint_id from the same author returns the existing entry with 200; the same key naming a different entry is 409 idempotency_key_reused; keys starting loopctl: are reserved.

Entry bodies and checkpoint notes are bounded by one module attribute that both the changeset and the OpenAPI operation reference, and refused with 422 secret_blocked when the secret denylist matches.

Callers write message entries only, from any principal of the tenant; review_requested, finding, fix and verdict belong to the review flow (US-45.3) and are refused with 422, and checkpoint, escalation and merge as loopctl's own. A checkpoint_id is cast to a canonical UUID and must name a checkpoint of the same story.
Every recorded checkpoint and entry appends an audit-chain event for the story in the same transaction; writes take a per-story advisory lock and the story FOR SHARE, reads take no lock.

GET /api/v1/stories/:id/thread returns the latest page of checkpoints with checkpoints_truncated, and one page of entries (after_seq, limit capped, next_after_seq), bodies marked untrusted, and 400 for a page parameter outside a non-negative int4 or a limit of 0; MCP tools thread_get, thread_checkpoint and thread_entry call the three endpoints, declared and dispatched, with a README row each naming every refusal, and send a checkpoint on the key claim_story claims with.
Tenant B cannot read or write tenant A's thread.

test_cases.name: checkpoint fence
steps: stale epoch; other agent; lapsed lease; review requested; reported done
expected_results: 409 stale_claim_epoch; 409 not_claimant; 409 claim_not_live for the last three

test_cases.name: replay rules
steps: resend a checkpoint and an entry; resend with different content; same commit under a new claim

test_cases.name: entry kinds and content
steps: finding, fix, verdict, checkpoint kinds; non-UUID and uppercase checkpoint_id; secret in body; reserved key

test_cases.name: audit and read
steps: record a checkpoint and a message; page the thread; out-of-range after_seq

test_cases.name: tenant isolation
steps: tenant B reads and writes tenant A's thread

technical_notes: Never cast tenant_id, story_id, seq, author_principal or dispatch_id.
Judgement kinds (finding, fix, verdict) and round counting belong to US-45.3: #901 tried to infer the judge's separation from the calling key and was circumvented at every review round.
The mcp-server route coverage test must see the new routes reached.
